correctness.rationale: The stated three-by-three Toeplitz compression is positive definite by a Fourier quadratic-form integral. Integration-by-parts establishes the opposite signs of its first and second offdiagonals in the superunit range and the strict inequality b>g. Symmetry reduces its exponential to a two-by-two hyperbolic block plus one antisymmetric scalar. Every diagonal and adjacent entry is positive. A convex two-exponential function H has H(0)=0, H'(0)=-2g<0, H''(t)>0 and H(t)→∞, proving exactly one positive recovery time for the only potentially negative entry. The isolated time t=0 remains positive. A uniform scaled Taylor expansion near alpha=1, together with g'(1)=Z/(4pi), gives both sharp boundary constants. The standalone final-package verifier passed 461 actual checks; analytic arguments, not these finite tests, establish all-parameter quantifiers.

value.rationale: Three consecutive interior sites form the minimal finite restricted stencil capable of exhibiting the known negative distance-two Fourier spectral coupling: a one- or two-site stencil cannot show that failure. Quantifying its exact semigroup recovery time determines when a discrete nonlocal heat approximation re-enters the nonnegative cone, resolving a gap left by qualitative negative-weight warnings and qualitative eventual-positivity theory. The linear-onset and quadratic-negative-depth boundary layer supplies a sharp small-order benchmark and a meaningful nontrivial finite cutoff. Neither general solver-wide nor floating-point significance is asserted.
